extracted.intended_audience: psychologists, researchers, and students who want to administer or reuse the Humor Styles Questionnaire (HSQ) in research or practice
extracted.subtask_description: Administration and scoring instructions for the Humor Styles Questionnaire (HSQ), a 32-item self-report scale that measures four humor-style dimensions. Includes item text, response scale, scoring code, reverse-keying rules, and citation/usage notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliative humor
rubrics_metrics.description: One of four HSQ dimensions (8 items). Examples of items: 'I usually don’t laugh or joke around much with other people.' (reverse), 'I don't have to work very hard at making other people laugh -- I seem to be a naturally humorous person.', 'I laugh and joke a lot with my friends.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored as the sum of items 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29 (see code: l: affiliative t: set - sum $hsq.1 $hsq.5 $hsq.9 $hsq.13 $hsq.17 $hsq.21 $hsq.25 $hsq.29). Range per dimension: 8-56.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-enhancing humor
rubrics_metrics.description: One of four HSQ dimensions (8 items). Examples of items: 'If I am feeling depressed, I can usually cheer myself up with humor.'; 'Even when I’m by myself, I’m often amused by the absurdities of life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored as the sum of items 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30 (see code: l: self_enhancing t: set - sum $hsq.2 $hsq.6 $hsq.10 $hsq.14 $hsq.18 $hsq.22 $hsq.26 $hsq.30). Range per dimension: 8-56.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggressive humor
rubrics_metrics.description: One of four HSQ dimensions (8 items). Examples of items: 'If someone makes a mistake, I will often tease them about it.'; 'When telling jokes or saying funny things, I am usually not very concerned about how other people are taking it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored as the sum of items 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 27, 31 (see code: l: aggressive t: set - sum $hsq.3 $hsq.7 $hsq.11 $hsq.15 $hsq.19 $hsq.23 $hsq.27 $hsq.31). Range per dimension: 8-56.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-defeating humor
rubrics_metrics.description: One of four HSQ dimensions (8 items). Examples of items: 'I let people laugh at me or make fun at my expense more than I should.'; 'I often go overboard in putting myself down when I am making jokes or trying to be funny.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored as the sum of items 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32 (see code: l: self_defeating t: set - sum $hsq.4 $hsq.8 $hsq.12 $hsq.16 $hsq.20 $hsq.24 $hsq.28 $hsq.32). Range per dimension: 8-56.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response scale (7-point Likert)
rubrics_metrics.description: The questionnaire uses a 7-point agreement scale with labeled anchors: 'totally disagree', 'moderately disagree', 'slightly disagree', 'neither agree nor disagree', 'slightly agree', 'moderately agree', 'totally agree'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each item is answered on this scale; reverse-keyed items must be reversed before summing for the relevant subscale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse-keyed items and coding convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Some HSQ items are reverse keyed (marked '{reverse}' in the item list). The page notes which numbered items are reverse keyed (items marked with * in the listing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reverse-keying mapping given: 'Items marked with * are reverse keyed; i.e., 1=7, 2=6, 3=5, 4=4, 5=3, 6=2, 7=1'. In the PsyToolkit code reverse items are indicated with '{reverse}'. Reverse items must be recoded prior to summing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring: items per dimension and score range
rubrics_metrics.description: For each of the four dimensions there are eight 7-item questions; dimension scores are sums of the eight items with possible range 8-56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page provides sample population means from Martin et al. (2003) and PsyToolkit sum-code snippets (l: affiliative/self_enhancing/aggressive/self_defeating). Use recoded reverse items before summing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration instructions / item prompt
rubrics_metrics.description: Introductory prompt: 'People experience and express humor in many different ways... Below is a list of statements describing different ways in which humor might be experienced. Please read each statement carefully, and indicate the degree to which you agree or disagree it. Please respond as honestly and objectively as you can.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administer as self-report; include the full prompt and response anchors; provide honest/objective responding instruction to participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission / citation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal/usage note: 'You can use the HSQ scale, as long as you acknowledge and cite the paper by Rod Martin and colleages.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reusing the scale in research or publications, cite: Martin, R.A., Puhlik-Doris, P., Larsen, G., Gray, J., and Weir, K. (2003). Individual differences in uses of humor and their relation to psychological well-being: Development of the Humor Styles Questionnaire. Journal of Research in Personality, 37, 48-75.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualization of 'sense of humor' (multiple dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sense of humor can be conceptualized as: a cognitive ability, an aesthetic response, a habitual behavior pattern, an emotion-related temperament trait, an attitude, and a coping strategy/defense mechanism (Martin, 2003).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conceptual framing supports interpretation: the HSQ focuses on styles (habitual/attitudinal/coping aspects) rather than only ability or aesthetic preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive vs negative dimension framing
rubrics_metrics.description: The HSQ measures two positive and two negative dimensions of humor: Affiliative and Self-enhancing (positive); Aggressive and Self-defeating (negative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of scores should consider valence: affiliative and self-enhancing styles are linked to adaptive outcomes, aggressive and self-defeating can be maladaptive (as discussed in the Martin et al. literature). The page reports sample sex differences (men scored higher than women on average in this sample).
